sentences.text: Ronald Keegan (Ron) is the person being assessed.
Lisa Keegan is Ronald's daughter and is present during the assessment.
The social worker, Tom Ashby, from the adult team at Coldmere, conducted the assessment.
The hospital requested a visit to assess Ronald's condition following a fall.
Ronald's wife, Pat, died in March of the previous year.
Ronald has difficulty managing stairs due to hip pain and stiffness.
Ronald uses his backside to go up stairs at night, as there is only one rail.
Ronald has a strip wash and cannot get into the bath due to the fall.
Lisa shops on Sundays for Ronald's meals.
Ronald prepares microwave dinners after Lisa shops.
Ronald used to attend the British Legion on Fridays but has not attended recently.
Ronald consumes alcohol, describing it as 'a couple of cans of an evening' with tea.
Lisa states Ronald drinks eight large cans of strong lager per day and has a bottle of vodka that is consumed in two days.
Lisa observes the empties of eight cans and a bottle of vodka in the bin every Sunday and counts them.
Ronald denies drinking excessively and states he is not drunk or hurting anyone.
Ronald agrees to consider a pendant alarm to call for help if he falls.
Ronald wishes to remain in his current home and does not want to move to a care home.
Mrs Okafor, next door, reported seeing Ronald drive to the Co-op after drinking.
Ronald denies driving after drinking and states he only drives on Sundays to the cemetery.
Ronald disputes that Mrs Okafor saw him driving and says she is 'trying to mind her own business'.
Ronald expressed concern about safety and stated that if unsure, he should not drive.
Ronald agrees to a home visit from the alcohol service for a single chat, not a meeting.
Ronald earns approximately £1,400 per month from state pension and works pension from the foundry.
Ronald does not currently receive Attendance Allowance.
Lisa agrees to help complete the Attendance Allowance form with Ronald.
The occupational therapist will assess stair rails and bathing needs.
The occupational therapist will conduct a bathing assessment by the second of December.
The social worker will write to Dr Haines at Bridge Street surgery about the falls and alcohol use with Ronald's consent.
The social worker will refer Ronald to the alcohol service this week and arrange a pendant alarm through Careline.
Lisa will complete the Attendance Allowance form with Ronald on Sunday.
